slide.title: One Page, Live Numbers
slide.body: Dashboard mock-up: scorecards 3,450 · 10 · 345 across the top; line chart and sorted bar chart below; date control top right. Small tag: AI-Powered Data Analysis · Lesson 10.

scenes.on_screen_text: One page, always up to date
scenes.voiceover: Every Monday, your manager asks for the latest numbers, and you copy charts into an email. A dashboard is one page, connected to your sheet, that people can open whenever they need it. Today, you build one.

slide.title: A Simple Dashboard in Looker Studio
slide.body: AI-Powered Data Analysis (No Code) · Lesson 10 of 14

scenes.voiceover: Last time, we built clear charts in Google Sheets. Now we bring them together on one page.

slide.title: How Looker Studio works
slide.body: Google Sheet → connector arrow → Looker Studio page with scorecards, charts, table. Circular arrow: sheet changes → dashboard updates.

scenes.voiceover: Looker Studio is a free Google tool for building dashboards and reports. It connects to a data source, such as a Google Sheet, and shows the data as charts, scorecards and tables on a page. When the sheet changes, the dashboard shows the new data.

slide.title: Four parts of a simple dashboard
slide.body: Wireframe: title bar across the top · date range control top right · row of scorecards · line chart (left) and bar chart (right) below. Each part labelled.

scenes.voiceover: A simple one-page dashboard has four parts. Scorecards, which are single large numbers, like total revenue. Charts, a line chart for change over time and a bar chart for comparisons. A filter control, like a date range, so viewers can choose the period. And a clear title with short labels, so the page makes sense without you.

slide.title: Where AI helps
slide.body: Calculated fields: e.g. average order value · Layout ideas: scorecards on top, charts below

scenes.voiceover: A calculated field is a new field that Looker Studio calculates from existing ones, for example average order value. AI can help you write the formula. AI can also suggest a layout, such as scorecards across the top and charts below.

slide.title: Share safely
slide.body: View-only access for named people · Check data source settings · Anonymised or approved data only (L02)

scenes.voiceover: Share safely. Give view-only access to named people, not edit access. Check the data source settings before you share, and only connect anonymised or approved data, as you learned in lesson two.

scenes.stock_query: car instrument panel speed and fuel
scenes.voiceover: A dashboard is like the instrument panel of a car. The driver does not need to see the engine. Only a few clear numbers, such as speed and fuel, always in the same place.

slide.title: Omar's data source (fictional)
slide.body: Clean 10-row orders table from content.md (Order ID 1001–1010, Order Date 2026-01-08 to 2026-03-25, Region, Product, Units, Unit Price, Revenue). Checklist beside it: one header row ✓ · no merged cells ✓ · real dates ✓. Caption: Omar · Amman

scenes.voiceover: Omar is a small business adviser in Amman, Jordan. He builds a dashboard for the fictional orders sheet, so the shop owner can check sales without opening the spreadsheet. The sheet has one header row, no merged cells, and real dates.

screen_steps: Open Looker Studio and choose Create > Report
In Add data to report, choose the Google Sheets connector
Select the orders spreadsheet and its worksheet
Keep 'Use first row as headers' ticked; click Add
scenes.voiceover: He opens Looker Studio and creates a new report. He chooses the Google Sheets connector, selects the spreadsheet and the worksheet, keeps the first row as headers, and adds it.

screen_steps: Open the data source fields; confirm Order Date is Date type and Revenue is Number (change if needed)
Add a scorecard with Revenue (SUM): 3,450
Add a second scorecard with Record Count: 10
scenes.voiceover: He checks the fields. Order date must be a date, and revenue must be a number. Then he adds two scorecards. Revenue shows three thousand four hundred and fifty, and the record count shows ten orders.

screen_steps: In Claude or ChatGPT type: 'Write a Looker Studio calculated field for average revenue per order, from fields Revenue and Order ID.'
Show the reply: SUM(Revenue) / COUNT(Order ID)
In Looker Studio, add a calculated field with this formula
Add a third scorecard with the new field: 345
Overlay the hand check: 3,450 ÷ 10 = 345 ✓
scenes.voiceover: Next, he asks the AI for a Looker Studio calculated field for average revenue per order. It suggests the sum of revenue divided by the count of order IDs. He adds it as a third scorecard, which shows three hundred and forty-five. He checks by hand. Three thousand four hundred and fifty divided by ten is three hundred and forty-five.

screen_steps: Add a time series chart
Set the dimension to Order Date, granularity Month
Set the metric to Revenue
Hover each point: 470, 820, 2,160
scenes.voiceover: Now the charts. First, a time series chart, with order date set to month, and revenue as the metric. It shows four hundred and seventy, eight hundred and twenty, and two thousand one hundred and sixty.

screen_steps: Add a bar chart
Dimension: Region; metric: Revenue; sort descending
Hover each bar: South 2,220, North 680, West 550
scenes.voiceover: Then a bar chart with region and revenue, sorted from largest. South is two thousand two hundred and twenty, North six hundred and eighty, and West five hundred and fifty.

screen_steps: Add a date range control and drag it to the top right
Switch to View mode
Set the range to 1–28 February 2026
Zoom on the Revenue scorecard: 820
scenes.voiceover: He adds a date range control in the top right, and tests it. He chooses February twenty twenty-six only, and total revenue changes to eight hundred and twenty.

screen_steps: Add a text box at the top: 'Orders dashboard, January to March 2026'
Click Share
Enter the placeholder address owner@example.com
Set the role to Viewer and send
scenes.voiceover: Finally, he types the title, orders dashboard, January to March twenty twenty-six. He clicks share, adds the owner's email address, and chooses viewer.

scenes.on_screen_text: Three to five numbers, not twelve charts
scenes.voiceover: A common mistake is to fill the page with every chart you can make. Twelve charts show nothing clearly. Choose the three to five numbers people really need, check each one against your pivot tables, and share with view-only access.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. Sheet → scorecards, charts, filters that update. 2. Keep it simple; check every number. 3. AI for layout and calculated fields; share view-only, safe data only.

scenes.voiceover: Let's recap. First, Looker Studio connects to a Google Sheet, and shows scorecards, charts and filters on a page that updates with the data. Second, keep it simple, and check every number against your sheet. Third, ask AI for layout ideas and calculated fields, and share with view-only access and only safe data.
